This commit introduces several new features and improvements to sqlite-web:

- **Image and Video Support:** The application now detects and displays images and videos stored as BLOBs in the database. This is handled by a new route that serves raw binary data with the correct content type, and new template filters that render the appropriate HTML tags.

- **UI Refresh:** The user interface has been updated with a modern stylesheet for a cleaner look and feel. This includes improved table styling, buttons, and a more consistent layout.

- **Easier to Use:** By displaying media directly in the browser, the application is now easier to use for databases containing images and videos.

- **Testing:** A new test suite has been added to verify the media display functionality. The dependencies in `requirements.txt` have also been updated to use the PyPI version of `peewee`.

- **.gitignore:** A `.gitignore` file has been added to exclude compiled Python files and other common temporary files from the repository.

author: phucxdoan
body:
As it turns out, database entries with tags with placeholder fields isn't a very useful feature. Apparently, every instance of substitution could just be replaced by an f-string if we map the expanded tag to the correct database entry.

In doing this, I realized that the MCU database could be vastly simpler. This whole tagging thing was an over-complication that probably made sense at the time.

So rather than having the MCU database be in the form of an S-expression that we then parse, we can just have a Python expression file that we evaluate. This allows for Python expression constructs that we can take advantage of to reduce duplication in the database. Furthermore, on my machine, the meta-preprocessing time went from ~0.100s to ~0.50s, so that's pretty good.

This can also set us up nicely for maybe parsing the CMSIS header to get the register fields automatically, at least a majority of them.

This fix addresses a bug where the build command was incorrectly including dependents through non-workspace components.

**Problem:** When a component was modified, the build would include not only direct dependents in the workspace but also dependents that were connected through components not present in the workspace.

# What does this implement/fix?

Adds an optional `interface` configuration variable to SPI-based ethernet types (W5500, DM9051, ENC28J60) allowing users to select the SPI host (`spi2` or `spi3`).

The variant-based SPI host selection has been moved from C++ preprocessor conditionals into Python validation, where it sets a sensible default per variant and allows the user to override it.

This is necessary when the default SPI interface collides with another component's choice. For example, the [board_m5cores3](https://github.com/m5stack/M5CoreS3-Esphome/tree/main/components/board_m5cores3) component uses SPI2_HOST on the ESP32-S3 for its display. When using a [CoreS3](https://docs.m5stack.com/en/core/CoreS3) with a [Base LAN PoE v1.2](https://docs.m5stack.com/en/base/lan_poe_v12), setting `interface: spi3` on the ethernet component resolves the conflict.

See [discussion](https://github.com/orgs/esphome/discussions/3281).

## Default SPI interface per variant

| Variant | Has SPI3 HW? | Old default | New default | Change? |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| ESP32 | yes | SPI3 | SPI3 | no |
| ESP32-S2 | yes | SPI2 | SPI2 | no |
| ESP32-S3 | yes | SPI2 | SPI2 | no |
| ESP32-C3 | no | SPI2 | SPI2 | no |
| ESP32-C5 | no | SPI2 | SPI2 | no |
| ESP32-C6 | no | SPI2 | SPI2 | no |
| ESP32-C61 | no | SPI2 | SPI2 | no |
| ESP32-H2 | no | SPI3 | SPI2 | **yes - bugfix** |
| ESP32-P4 | yes | SPI3 | SPI2 | **yes** |

ESP32-H2 was broken before — the old C++ code defaulted to SPI3 but the hardware only has SPI2. ESP32-P4 has SPI3 hardware but the old code only defaulted to SPI3 by accident (it wasn't in the `#if` variant list); users can explicitly set `interface: spi3` on P4 if needed.
